title: Bran Flakezz on Winning ‘Unwell Summer Games,’ His Future With Reality TV and the Alex Cooper-Alix Earle Drama
description:
Bran Flakezz is anything but “Unwell.”

	Brandon Edelman, better known as Bran Flakezz online, just emerged as one of four winners of the “Unwell Su
body:
Bran Flakezz is anything but “Unwell.”

	Brandon Edelman, better known as Bran Flakezz online, just emerged as one of four winners of the “Unwell Summer Games” on YouTube, created through Alex Cooper’s “Unwell” network. The four-episode series brought 16 content creators together at a luxury ranch in Canada to compete in a series of challenges for a chance to win a share of $250,000, with the prize money distributed throughout the four days of the competition.
	

	“There’s just so many exciting things happening that sometimes I do have to remind myself to take a step back,” Edelman tells Variety as he gets ready to speak at a Forbes CMO summit in Aspen, Colo.


	Unlike a traditional competition series, “Unwell Summer Games” puts a group of established content creators — many of whom already knew each other — in the same house, ensuring there would be no shortage of drama. In the final episode, the contestants split into four teams for a final challenge. Edelman took home $25,000, alongside Jourdan Riane, Blake Gray and Carly Sutherland Lawrence, the last of whom had a less-than-perfect relationship with Bran on the show.

	“There is a very funny moment where, after we scream at each other, we end up on the same team for the final challenge, and then we proceed to win the show together,” Edelman says, laughing. “Her and I have a very crazy storyline.”

	Edelman got his start posting transparent videos on social media, detailing everything from his life in Philadelphia to the financial realities of being a content creator through his “TikTok Transparency” series. He’s since amassed more than 1 million followers on TikTok and made Forbes’ 30 Under 30 list in Social Media.
	

	After working as a fitting room employee at Forever 21, Edelman went on to compete on Barstool’s “Project Verified” and is now part of Michelle Obama’s Gen Z voter registration intitiative. And after winning the “Unwell Summer Games,” he says he’s just getting started.

	Below, Edelman talks to Variety about his time on “Unwell Summer Games,” his future in reality TV and his take on the Alex Cooper and Alix Earle drama.
	
		Will we see you doing more reality TV after this?	

	Never say never. I think it’s always a case by case situation. As much as I love “Big Brother,” that’s a three-month filming schedule. Three months without posting online for me would be super detrimental, so that would be difficult. I love “Survivor.” No way in hell will you have me on an island like eating rice and sand. I think right now, anything that I want to do in a potential reality TV space is just make something that’s meaningful and real. Something I’ve always noticed when I watch reality TV is that a lot of things feel so overproduced, and that’s not what I want to do. Something that I loved about this show is that none of this drama was manufactured. This truly was how everything played out, and these people’s feelings are very real. That was really refreshing to me.
	
		This isn’t a normal competition show. It’s a house full of content creators. Do you think that having that affected the dynamic and led to some drama?	

	100%. A lot of us had either been friends, met before or, in some circumstances, were exes. These are all people that have a platform, and you’ve probably seen their content. So your first impression of them is, “Oh, I’ve been watching that guy’s videos for three years. He seems like a D-bag online. I wonder how he’s going to be in real life.” I probably had met over half that cast before we walked in there.
	
		Do you still stay in touch with people from the show?	

	Yeah, it’s great. We have a big group chat that’s always popping off, especially right now, because the show is actually airing. We’re all like, “Oh my gosh, you said this in your interview,” or, “Oh my gosh, I can’t believe they put this in that sequence, or they cut this part out.”
	
		Are you watching the drama and thinking, “Oh, I didn’t know she said this”?	

	Definitely. My first reality show [Barstool’s “Project Verified”], I feel like people were talking about me in their interviews, and they probably did talk about me on this show and it just didn’t make the cut. And thank you to the editors for that, because I have a fragile ego. There were definitely some things where I was like, “Oh wow, that person said that about that person. I didn’t realize that.” And even sometimes I will see myself say something and go, “That was kind of mean, Brandon.” But it’s TV, and when you’re in a situation like that, it is a pressure cooker.
	
	
		You became somewhat of a fan favorite while on “Unwell Summer Games.” People online are saying you were the perfect blend of loving drama but still being an empath.	

	They did mention that I was the only person out of all 16 of us that was in a relationship, so my strategy going into it was that I’m going to be a matchmaker. I’m going to help the girls go after the guys that they want. I just wanted to be a safe space for everybody, and have fun.
	
		It was interesting, because you were interested in the drama on the show, but you were never directly involved in any.	

	We all flew out here and we’re working for four days. I didn’t want this to be us all sitting in a circle playing Kumbaya. I definitely wanted there to be realness and honesty. It’s not like I was like, “Everyone needs to fight.” But I was like, ”You want to hook up with that guy? Go for it. This is the time.”
	
		I have to ask about the Blake, Zarah and Carly love triangle. What was it like seeing that unfold in real time?	

	It was complicated, because I liked all three of them so much. You kind of see in my conversation with Zarah that I just wanted her to be very honest with me about her feelings with Blake, and then act on them. My motto in life is always say what you mean and mean what you say, and that’s where I kind of guided her a little bit. And I was like, “If you said this whole time that you really care about Blake and you want to pursue something with him, or your feelings are still there, then it’s one thing to confront Carly, but you have been telling everybody you don’t want any part of this.” I wanted to be a friend for her in that moment, and be like, “Why don’t you take a step back and really reassess?” 

	In Zarah’s defense, though, I do think Carly was a little bit scattered. I was really surprised with Carly, because she was also someone who said she wasn’t going to kiss anybody, and then she goes for Blake. She was obsessed with Chad. Then she goes to Tim. I think it’s complicated when you have someone like Blake who is younger and such a genuine guy. But I think he’s there to have fun and doesn’t necessarily want to be in drama either.
	
		In the finale, there’s a moment where you yell at Carly.	

	Episode 3 ends with me trying to shake Carly and say, “I think a lot of your feelings are valid, but you control how you react to the situation. If you feel like Suede, Zarah and Hallie are excluding you, that’s three out of 16 members of this cast. Maybe you should say, “I’m not vibing with those girls. I’m going to hang out with Brandon, Cassie and Daniela.’” She is playing victim a little bit, and I just wanted her to make the best of this experience and just have fun. This is a silly little show. We leave tomorrow.
	

	One thing they didn’t show me say to her was, “You’re upset that you’re not being picked for anyone’s team, but have you even gone up to any of the captains and say, ‘Hey, I would love to work with you?’ And she’s like, ‘Well, no.’” I said, “You almost expect things to fall on your plate, and when they don’t, you kind of throw your hands up in the air.” It takes two people to communicate. She was just looking at the glass half empty. 

	What you’ll see in the fourth episode is that pressure-cooker moment of me reaching my breaking point because of how she lashed out a little bit on Chad. When people are hurt, they tend to push away the people that they’re closest to, and I think that day Carly was like, “Oh, Bran’s mad at me.” She was talking to everybody else but me, and I wasn’t mad at her. I was just frustrated with her because I loved her so much. I blew a fuse for sure. And it’s not something that I’m proud of. I definitely never want to yell at anybody, let alone a woman.
	
		How does it feel to win a reality show?	

	It feels incredible. One of my favorite “Survivor” players of all time is Cirie Fields, and she did a very infamous speech where she was like, “My mother always said, ‘You may not be able to beat them with these [points to his arms], but you can beat them with this [points to his brain]. And I tied that into my experience. I was like, “I might not beat you in a race, but I will beat you in brain power.”
	
		I have to ask you this. You were just on Alex Cooper’s show. We also saw you at Alix Earle’s “Earle Meets World” premiere. Have you been keeping up with the drama?	

	I will say, I wish we had more fascination with men than we do with women. These are two very successful, powerful women, and everyone just wants to push this narrative of beef and controversy and picking teams. I personally feel like both of them are incredible and super amazing at what they do, and I think one of those elements that both of them have is they’ll never take a business opportunity away from a mutual friend.

	This interview has been edited and condensed.

schema.headline: Bran Flakezz on Winning ‘Unwell Summer Games,’ His Future With Reality TV and the Alex Cooper-Alix Earle Drama

title: Benjamin Netanyahu Calls to ‘Revoke the Citizenship’ of ‘Anyone Who Slanders IDF Soldiers’ Following ‘NAZA’ Documentary Premiere
description: Following the premiere of “NAZA” at the Venice Film Festival earlier this month, Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is calling for the intro
body:
Following the premiere of “NAZA” at the Venice Film Festival earlier this month, Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is calling for the introduction of a law that would “revoke the citizenship of anyone who slanders IDF [Israeli Defense Forces] soldiers.”

	“We will hit them in their pockets and also in their citizenship, because their place is not among us,” he said in a video posted to X on Wednesday. He went on to describe another law that would raise “the defamation damages they can be sued for twentyfold.”
	

	“NAZA,” co-directed by Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, who are both Israeli citizens, shows “in detail the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza,” according to its official logline. The film features interviews with 24 Israeli military intelligence officers and soldiers.


	The documentary won the special jury prize at the festival, and also received a 24.5-minute standing ovation — the longest in the festival’s history. 

	Netanyahu’s statement comes following the words of Israel’s Minister of Culture Miki Zohar, who threatened to revoke the Israeli citizenships of Abraham and Szor on Sunday. He called the documentary “shocking” and accused the filmmakers of “betraying the state.”

	“The self-loathing that burns in the creators, who are willing to harm their homeland just to get applause from antisemites around the world, is inconceivable and constitutes a betrayal of the state,” Zohar wrote. “As Minister of Culture, I will act immediately to revoke the Israeli citizenship of these despicable creators for betraying the state.”

schema.headline: Benjamin Netanyahu Calls to ‘Revoke the Citizenship’ of ‘Anyone Who Slanders IDF Soldiers’ Following ‘NAZA’ Documentary Premiere

title: Ed Sheeran Backlash Explodes as Ms. Rachel, Hannah Einbinder and More Slam Singer After Macklemore Dropped From Tour: ‘Silence During a Genocide Is Not Neutral’
description: Voices across Hollywood and Washington are speaking out after Macklemore was dropped from Ed Sheeran’s Loop Tour for making pro-Palestine comments o
body:
Voices across Hollywood and Washington are speaking out after Macklemore was dropped from Ed Sheeran’s Loop Tour for making pro-Palestine comments on stage.

	“Hacks” star Hannah Einbinder, one of TV’s most politically outspoken stars, wrote on her Instagram stories on Tuesday, “Ed Sheeran i say this as a ginger. i hope you get a REALLY bad sun burn. the kind on the back of your entire body where it hurts to lie down or walk or sit.”
	

	YouTuber and children’s entertainer Ms. Rachel also took to Instagram to call out Sheeran. She wrote on Monday, “Ed Sheeran had an opportunity [to] show that we won’t be bullied into punishing people for supporting Palestine. Instead he caved to people who refuse to accept what the world knows. A genocide is happening in Gaza. We all need to speak out against it.”


	She added, “If more than 20,000 white children were killed in another part of the world, everyone would be shouting about it at their concerts. Treating some children’s lives as less worthy of outrage is racist. Silence during a genocide is not neutral.”

	“Wicked” star Marissa Bode, who is in a wheelchair, said in a TikTok video, “Ed Sheeran, my legs may not work like they used to before, but at least I have a fucking spine. Free Palestine, bitch!”

	Sen. Bernie Sanders posted a statement on X, slamming New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft, whom Macklemore partially blamed for his removal from the Loop Tour in a statement about his exit. “In the United States of America, billionaire stadium owners should not be able to silence artists because they speak out on political issues. Today it is the genocide in Gaza. What’s next? If they can silence one artist, they can silence anyone,” Sanders wrote.
	

	On Sept. 4, Macklemore sang out “Free Palestine” during his set at New Jersey’s MetLife Stadium. The comments made headlines, and the rapper was removed from Sheeran’s Loop Tour on Sept. 14. The same day, Macklemore released a lengthy statement on Instagram explaining his side of the story. He wrote, “Last Monday, in the middle of all the media attention surrounding Pink and what I said at MetLife, Ed told me that Robert Kraft called him. We were scheduled to play Gillette Stadium later this month, which is owned by the Kraft Group. Ed told me that Kraft said I would not be allowed to perform in his stadium. Ed also told me that Kraft had rallied some of the other stadium owners and collectively they gave him an ultimatum: if Macklemore stays on the tour, you will not be allowed to play in our venues.”

	He added, “Ed was in a fucked up position. He knew it. His typical apolitical stance was being challenged in a way it never had been before. He told me that the words ‘Free Palestine’ and the image of the Palestinian flag were hurtful to a lot of people he spoke with. I told him that if those words were more offensive than tens of thousands of Palestinian children being killed by Israel, then there was a fundamental disconnect between where those people stood and where I stood. But he couldn’t get past his public facing, ‘I don’t take sides.’”

	On Sept. 15, Sheeran released his own statement. He claimed that he spoke with venue owners “at length all week to try and build a bridge” after Macklemore’s comments. Sheeran also asserted that dropping Macklemore was “the promoter’s decision, it was not mine.”

	“I would never let down the fans who had made plans, nor would I abandon the touring crew and the other support acts and musicians who rely on me for work and to make a living,” he added.

	Despite Sheeran’s comments, openers Finneas, Aaron Rowe, Lukas Graham and Irish band Beoga all left the tour after Macklemore was dropped.

	On Wednesday, Macklemore announced that he will donate the $1 million net earnings he received from the Loop Tour to organizations that support the Palestinian people.

	“With everything that has happened over the last 48 hours, I want to bring the conversation back to where it belongs: to the Palestinian people who are still being killed, still living under military occupation, and still fighting for their freedom,” he wrote on Instagram. “I will be donating the entire $1 million of my net earnings from Ed Sheeran’s Loop Tour to six organizations working directly to support the Palestinian people. And I invite Robert Kraft to match my donation. Whatever we disagree about, perhaps we can agree on this: Palestinian lives are worth protecting. A Palestinian life is no less valuable than any other life on this earth.”
	

	Shortly after Macklemore’s announcement, Kraft put out a statement saying that he and Sheeran are donating $2 million each to the Palestinian cause. The statement, released on the Gillette Stadium X account, read, “I have dedicated much of my life to building bridges between all people. I believe deeply that all lives are worth protecting. Earlier today, before Macklemore challenged me to match his donation, Ed called me and asked me to commit $2 million to match his donation to aid in the region to fight this humanitarian crisis. Ed now plans to reach out to other venue owners and our goal is to continue to work together to build bridges”

schema.headline: Ed Sheeran Backlash Explodes as Ms. Rachel, Hannah Einbinder and More Slam Singer After Macklemore Dropped From Tour: ‘Silence During a Genocide Is Not Neutral’

title: Flamingo Estate’s Richard Christiansen on Pamela Anderson’s Pickles, Julianne Moore’s Honey and the Dolly Parton Coffee That ‘Got Away’
description: Richard Christiansen was working in the offices at Flamingo Estate, his farm and lifestyle brand in the Highland Park neighborhood of Los Angeles, w
body:
Richard Christiansen was working in the offices at Flamingo Estate, his farm and lifestyle brand in the Highland Park neighborhood of Los Angeles, when Pamela Anderson’s son, Brandon Lee, called him to ask if he’d be interested in collaborating with his mother.

	“He said, ‘Would you like to do something with my mom? She’s a big gardener,’” Christiansen recalls. “They don’t have the same surname, so I didn’t know who he was talking about so I was like, ‘OK, who’s your mom?’ He said, ‘Pamela Anderson.’ I was like, ‘Holy shit!”
	

	At that point, Flamingo Estate was making a name for itself, among other things, for its celeb honey collaborations. Christiansen had already partnered with Julianne Moore and LeBron James to create their limited-edition lines of honey. All Flamingo Estate celebrity partnerships benefit not-for-profits. The celebs do not get paid for their work.


	When Anderson arrived for their first meeting, Christiansen gave her his customary honey pitch. “I wanted her to do a honey, like many of the ones we’ve done,” says Christiansen, who grew up on a bee farm in Australia. “Honey’s easy for us. I take my hives to someone’s house to do. Like we tied them to LeBron’s roof or for Ed Ruscha recently, we put the hives in his studio. Julianne Moore’s honey was from her garden in Montauk. It’s some of the best. It’s dark and it’s almost molasses, like whisky.”

	But Anderson had another idea. “She said matter-of-factly, ‘I want to do pickles with you. It’s my aunt’s recipe,’” Christiansen says. Anderson’s $38 jars of pickles raised $500,000 for the California Wildlife Center.
	



	

	



	I am talking to Christiansen on Zoom shortly before the release of his new book, “Pleasure Principles.” The gorgeously illustrated and designed 408-page tome, subtitled “An Almanac from the Garden,” features recipes, DIY projects and musings on a range of topics from the cinematic history of the moon to celebrity restaurants in L.A.

	If anything, “Pleasure Principles” serves as a look inside Christiansen’s very creative and colorful mind. “I don’t have a car,” he explains. “I ride my bicycle everywhere, and when I’m on my bike, I dictate into my phone. That’s maybe why everything’s short, these short little stories.”



	

	



	Christiansen’s latest Hollywood collaboration is a first for him, a movie tie-in with “Practical Magic 2.” Not only do several Flamingo Estate products, including bottles of olive oil and Green Goddess candles, appear in the movie, but Christiansen has also curated a gift box inspired by the Nicole Kidman and Sandra Bullock film.

	It’s a few days after Dolly Parton passed away in August. I ask Christiansen to name a celebrity he’d love to work with. “We were going to do a coffee with Dolly called ‘8 to 6’ instead of ‘9 to 5,’” he says. “We had some lovely conversations about it, and then it didn’t end up happening because we were too young at that point and our distribution probably couldn’t handle the weight of her reach. That was the one that got away.”

schema.headline: Flamingo Estate’s Richard Christiansen on Pamela Anderson’s Pickles, Julianne Moore’s Honey and the Dolly Parton Coffee That ‘Got Away’

title: Paramount May Be Bluffing About Leaving California, but L.A. Mayor Taking It Seriously
description:
Paramount has been threatening to leave California since July, when the state sued to block it from merging with Warner Bros. Discovery.

	Attorney
body:
Paramount has been threatening to leave California since July, when the state sued to block it from merging with Warner Bros. Discovery.

	Attorney General Rob Bonta has called it “blackmail” meant to stop him from enforcing antitrust law. But Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass, for one, is taking the threat seriously and is trying to do whatever she can to persuade the company to stay.

	“We’ve heard the same information that everybody has,” said Steve Kang, the mayor’s film czar, on Wednesday. “We need to be prepared for every option to be available — whether it’s true or not.”
	

	Paramount faces an Oct. 1 deadline to close its transaction or begin accruing a $7-million-a-day “ticking fee” owed to WBD shareholders. In recent days, the noise about a potential relocation has started to pick up with reports in Politico and TMZ that the company is taking affirmative steps toward a move.


	Bass has already done most of what she can do, urging Bonta last month to come to the table and reach a deal. 

	Bonta’s office has repeatedly said that it is open to good faith talks, but has said it will only agree to a resolution that includes “robust structural remedies.” A court-supervised settlement conference has been set for Oct. 14-15.

	In a statement on Wednesday, Bonta’s office said the threat to move out of California is nothing new.

	“We cannot comment on a company’s plans,” the A.G.’s office said. “It’s no secret that Paramount has been making this threat, despite its alleged commitment to California and Hollywood. What Paramount decides to do is Paramount’s choice alone. We’ll continue to apply the law without fear or favor and continue to be open to coming to the table for good faith discussions.”
	

	Paramount declined to comment.

	Kang was appointed in 2025 to serve as Bass’ liaison to the film community. Asked what steps Bass could take, aside from pressuring Bonta, to get Paramount to stay, Kang cited her support for increased subsidies for production in California and in Washington, D.C.

	“Creating a film-friendly environment is our first and foremost priority,” he said. “We’re hoping they don’t leave. We’re hoping all sides are speaking to one another. This is an issue between the attorney general and Paramount. All we can do is encourage discussions among all parties.”

schema.headline: Paramount May Be Bluffing About Leaving California, but L.A. Mayor Taking It Seriously

title: Celebrity Wedding Planner Mindy Weiss Says "I Do" to New Ring Pop Candy Collaboration
description:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

	If there’
body:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

	If there’s one thing celebrity wedding planner Mindy Weiss knows, it’s how to create a moment.

	Now, the woman behind the recent wedding of Selena Gomez and Benny Blanco, plus weddings and parties for Finneas, Justin Bieber and The Kardashians is putting her touch on Ring Pop, the popular candy brand known for its colorful ring-shaped suckers.

	While Ring Pop has helped people pop the question since the 80s, Weiss has teamed up with the brand for The Wedding Collection, to unveil Ring Pops that help people say “I Do!”


		

						
			
	

					Amazon
	
					
		

										NEW RELEASE						

					Ring Pop Wedding Collection Lollipops		

	
		50-count pack	
		
	

	The new Ring Pop release features the mini lollipops in three romance-inspired flavors: “First Kiss” watermelon; “Main Squeeze” citrus; and “Berry in Love” strawberry. Each Ring Pop is wrapped like a wedding favor, with occasion-appropriate sayings adorning the packaging (think phrases like “Off the Market,” “Ring it On” and “I Said Yes”).

	And just so you don’t ruin your first kiss, Ring Pop says The Wedding Collection features “lighter-toned gems” that are designed to not stain your lips or teeth.



	

									Tim Chan
	



	Weiss was tapped as the creative director for the collection, and the event planner helped with everything from the packaging design to the gemstone colors. She says she was excited to offer another way for couples to create a memorable moment on their big day.

	“Behind every wedding I’ve planned, there’s a detail that makes guests stop and smile because it’s something unexpected that feels personal,” Weiss says in a release. “Ring Pop already had that magic and couples were finding their own way to use them long before we started this collection. My job was simply to give it the packaging, the polish and the occasions it deserved. This is Ring Pop, all grown up, but still exactly as fun as you remember it.”


	“Ring Pop has always been a symbol of celebration, and lately, of love,” adds Joanna Firestone, Marketing Director at Bazooka Brands. “Over the years, we’ve watched Ring Pop organically become part of the wedding journey — engagements, bachelorettes, showers, weddings. With the wedding industry booming and packaging aesthetics mattering more to consumers than ever, it felt like the right moment to make it official. And there was no better partner than celebrity wedding planner Mindy Weiss.”

	The Ring Pop Wedding Collection launches exclusively in stores at David’s Bridal and online on Amazon, which has 15-count and 50-count bags of Ring Pops available here.

schema.headline: Celebrity Wedding Planner Mindy Weiss Says "I Do" to New Ring Pop Candy Collaboration

title: ‘Charlie’s Angels’ Star Jaclyn Smith on the Emmys Reunion, ‘Snobbism’ Against the Series and Why the Latest Movie Reboot ‘Didn’t Work’
description: The Television Academy may have celebrated the 50th anniversary of “Charlie’s Angels” at the Emmys on Monday night with an onstage reunion of the sh
body:
The Television Academy may have celebrated the 50th anniversary of “Charlie’s Angels” at the Emmys on Monday night with an onstage reunion of the show’s stars Jaclyn Smith, Kate Jackson and Cheryl Ladd, but the TV organization wasn’t as generous to the Aaron Spelling series when it originally aired in the 70s.

	“Charlie’s Angels” received only four Emmy nominations and no wins during its five-season run from 1976 to 1981. Jackson earned two acting nods and David Doyle, who played Bosley, was nominated once. A sound editing nomination was picked up in 1977.
	

	“It would have been nice to have gotten Emmys, but there was a snobbism about it,” Smith told me Wednesday. “They didn’t like all the glamor. They put us down. We were Barbie dolls. They didn’t see the weight or the depth of the devotion of the girls to each other. They thought it was fluff, and Aaron said, ‘It’s eye candy.’ But he also gave it narrative. He gave it mystery. He gave enough danger to keep you leaning forward. It had a little bit of everything.”


	Little did most anyone know back then that “Charlie’s Angels” would go on to have a multigenerational fanbase for a half-century.

	Farrah Fawcett played Jill Munroe with Smith as Kelly Garrett and Jackson as Sabrina Duncan. Ladd joined the series as Jill’s sister, Kris Munroe, after Fawcett left the show following the first season due to contract disputes with Spelling. John Forsythe was the voice of Charlie, the Angels’ boss who was never seen on screen.

	Ladd says their off-screen camaraderie mimicked what TV audiences saw on the small screen. “We were women that were completely for each other. We weren’t like, ‘I’m better than you,’” she says. “There was no fighting. I thought that was just such a great way to bring women together and to give them strength.”
	

	Earlier this year, Smith, Jackson and Ladd appeared at a 50-year celebration at PaleyFest in Los Angeles. “It was emotional in the sense that so many years had gone by, and it reminds you of the passage of time, of course, and that we don’t have Farrah, David Doyle and John Forsythe,” Smith says. “Those were important people and people I love, certainly. But it’s still rewarding to think that when something has some magic, it’s lasting and it still brings joy to many generations.”

	Ladd says of their Emmys reunion, “There was a lot of love in that room for us, and I really appreciated that. I could feel it.”

	Smith, who is currently on a nationwide tour promoting her new memoir “I Once Knew a Guy Named Charlie,” says she enjoyed the two “Charlie ‘Angels” movies in 2000 and 2003 that starred Drew Barrymore, Cameron Diaz and Lucy Liu. “Drew kept to that winning concept. She took it a step further. She evolved it,” Smith says. “She did it beautifully. It was more spectacular. It was diving off buildings, escaping explosions and still tongue in cheek.”

	While Smith calls Elizabeth Banks a “great and talented” filmmaker, she’s not surprised that her 2019 “Charlie’s Angel” movie, toplined by Kristen Stewart, Naomi Scott and Ella Balinska, failed to reach audiences. “She tried to really do a departure, and it didn’t work because what I find is if people love something, they don’t want it to change that much,” Smith says. “They want the original idea. But this had several Bosleys. The girls didn’t get along. Our whole essence was, we were a sisterhood, a fellowship. We had each other. It was loyalty before romance. We used our sex appeal to help us, and yet it still had a strong feminist backbone. I think it changed women’s roles on television.”

schema.headline: ‘Charlie’s Angels’ Star Jaclyn Smith on the Emmys Reunion, ‘Snobbism’ Against the Series and Why the Latest Movie Reboot ‘Didn’t Work’

title: Jessica Chastain to Star in New Netflix Drama Series ‘The Retrievals’
description:
Jessica Chastain has joined Netflix’s “The Retrievals,” a new drama series from the streamer.

	The Oscar-winning actor will star as Kaitlyn Langfor
body:
Jessica Chastain has joined Netflix’s “The Retrievals,” a new drama series from the streamer.

	The Oscar-winning actor will star as Kaitlyn Langford, a former art historian who has “spent the last decade stuck in an endless cycle of failed fertility treatments,” per Netflix. “When she learns she’s also a victim of criminal drug diversion at the Yale Fertility Center, she faces a devastating personal reckoning and becomes a key plaintiff in this historic lawsuit against Yale.”
	

	Chastain “was the writing team’s ‘exemplar’ while crafting the role of Kaitlyn,” said showrunner, writer and executive producer Molly Smith Metzler. “As a performer, she has the rare ability to convey extreme restraint and unbridled freefall, often at the same time. It gives me goosebumps just thinking about what Jessica’s going to do with this role.”


	Chastain joins previously announced cast members Emilia Jones and Amy Ryan.

	As previously reported by Variety, the show will follow “an unlikely community of IVF patients who come together to crusade against Yale University after they are operated on without anesthesia — because a nurse stole their fentanyl.”

	“The Retrievals” is based on the New York Times and Serial Productions podcast of the same name by Susan Burton.

	In addition to Metzler, the series is executive produced by Dani Gorin, Tom Ackerley, and Margot Robbie for LuckyChap; Colin McKenna (“Maid,” “Sirens”), Caitlin Roper for The New York Times, and podcast writer Susan Burton. The project is produced by LuckyChap and Quiet Coyote. Lila Neugebauer (“Maid,” “Sirens,” “The Beast in Me”) serves as the pilot director and executive producer.

title: The AI Race, the Search for Sticky Content and Building Fan Communities on the Agenda at Variety’s Entertainment and Technology Summit
description: Is the stock market in the grip of an AI bubble? Will consumer spending collapse under the weight of inflation fueled by rising energy prices? Can D
body:
Is the stock market in the grip of an AI bubble? Will consumer spending collapse under the weight of inflation fueled by rising energy prices? Can Disney, Netflix and other entertainment giants build out their streaming platforms beyond video to boost profits and margins?

	There’s no shortage of business trends coalescing around media and entertainment as its industry leaders converge Sept. 17 in Los Angeles for Variety’s annual Entertainment and Technology Summit, presented by EY.
	

	Hollywood is grappling yet again with a fresh cycle of technology-driven upheaval in its operations and business models. The dawning potential of generative AI promises to radically change how movies and TV shows are made. And the distribution systems of tomorrow are not as lucrative as the pay-TV ecosystems of the previous half-century.


	Javi Borges, global Americas media and entertainment sector leader for accounting and consulting giant EY, asserts that entertainment companies need to also understand the sea change that is afoot in consumer tastes for leisure-time pursuits.

	“We’re seeing a shift from event-driven experiences to connected community experiences. The consumer is the fan. You want to shift from having consumers to having fans and loyal supporters that interact with your product, with your experience on an ongoing basis,” says Borges, a 27-year veteran of EY. “That’s why you see the prioritization of sports in some of the media rights negotiations and in the valuations that we’re seeing in the market. It’s because of the stickiness of the fan.”
	



	

					EY’s Javi Borges
	



	The AI effect on the stock market has cast a big shadow over media and tech shares. Borges sees a bumpy period of adjustment in the short term as the industry sorts out processes to ensure that human creatives still oversee the work of AI’s crafty agents.

	“The unique aspect about AI is the speed of change that we’re seeing is unprecedented. With technology, the time frame between major breakthroughs gets shorter and the change gets faster,” Borges says. “The speed of change and the speed of evolution around it, that’s what drives a lot of nervousness.”

	But the potential for AI to boost the productivity of the humans that use AI tools can’t be denied.“We think that AI is an opportunity to really have people do more and we think that there’s going to be economic growth because of it,” Borges says. “The right governance needs to be put in place. But I think it democratizes the cost of filmmaking.”

	One concerning macroeconomic trend on the horizon that could impact the entertainment sector even more than AI in the near term is the pressure on consumer prices. The war in Iran and the ripple effects of on-again, off-again tariffs and related supply chain disruptions are seen at the supermarket and the gas pump and everywhere else consumers feel the sting of rising prices. Layoffs in key sectors such as tech, banking and entertainment have also put pressure on pocketbooks. The wobbliness of consumer spending coupled with a steady decline in the rate of personal savings held by the average American has raised red flags for entertainment sector economists.

	“The U.S. media & entertainment business is consumer-centric, and changes in the health of the American consumer directly impacts the companies playing in this space,” wrote Robert Fishman, media and entertainment analyst for MoffettNathanson Research, in a July report. “Today, elevated fuel costs, persistent core inflation above the Fed target and a depleting savings buffer should all serve as warning flags for consumer spending.”

	Strong consumer spending is crucial for the latest strategic wave around subscription video that Disney, NBCUniversal and others are embracing. Both companies have articulated a vision for Disney+ and Peacock, respectively, to grow beyond video subscriptions to serve as a funnel for attracting consumers with theme parks and opportunities for experiences. The idea is to thread other Disney and NBCUniversal products and services into the streaming platforms, making them a hub of companywide activity.
	

	Disney plans to roll out elements of what CEO Josh D’Amaro called “this expanded ecosystem” to its 131 million Disney+ subscribers worldwide by next spring, as the exec told Wall Street analysts in August.“As we look to make Disney+ the digital centerpiece of our relationships with fans, we’re just playing a different game” from other rivals, D’Amaro said in outlining his vision for Disney+.

	EY’s Borges sees the initiative at Disney and elsewhere as indicative of the importance of keeping connected with fans and bringing them one-of-a-kind experiences or can’t-miss movies and TV shows that help keep them loyal to their favorite brands.

	“We’re really in a period where there is immense value in having a streaming platform, and it’s being manifested in different ways. The common thread that you see is the extension of the IP into a connected experience,” Borges says. “So whether that’s in a community setting or cross- leveraging audiences like Netflix running the ‘GTA 6’ preview, you’re seeing that kind of connectivity. I think where things are headed for entertainment is going to revolve and two things: The continued extension of IP and the connectivity to the community around the product.”

	***
	
		Bellwethers of the Business	

	Five market-pacing companies to watch as 2026 winds down

	NetflixStock performance year to date: down 19%

	The streaming leader faces investors questions about long-term growth drivers after the aborted M&A effort earlier this year with Warner Bros. Discovery. Netflix is counting on subscriber gains from outside the U.S., plus a larger menu of sports and live events to drive big advertising sales.

	DisneyStock performance year to date: down 6%

	The Mouse House needs consumer spending to stay strong to keep its parks, cruises and experiences operations humming. New CEO Josh D’Amaro is touting the cross-platform marketing benefits of threading more Disney priorities into the Disney+ ecosystem.

	Canal+Stock performance year to date: down 5%

	France’s biggest pay-TV company is becoming a proxy stock for Europe’s growing swagger across the global media marketplace. Canal+ is investing big in original French film production in exchange for favorable home-field advantage rules around exhibition in theaters and on streaming.
	

	ComcastStock performance year to date: down 15%

	The Philadelphia-based media giant is on track to split its cable and broadband assets and NBCUniversal into separate companies by mid-2027. After more than 15 years together, the shift will put pressure on the studio, NBC and Peacock to perform in the eyes of investors.

	NvidiaStock performance year to date: up 15%

	If AI catches a cold, Nvidia gets pneumonia. The chipmaker’s stock will reflect any softening of demand or enthusiasm for the AI revolution that has fueled the vast majority of U.S. equity gains in recent quarters.

	(Source: Variety research. Year-to-date: Jan. 2-Sept. 16)

title: ‘Neagley’ Cast Guide: Meet All the Characters From Prime Video’s New ‘Reacher’ Spinoff
description:
Sep 16, 2026 4:00pm PT	
	

	
		‘Neagley’ Cast Guide: Meet All the Characters From Prime Video’s New ‘Reacher’ Spinoff
body:
Sep 16, 2026 4:00pm PT	
	

	
		‘Neagley’ Cast Guide: Meet All the Characters From Prime Video’s New ‘Reacher’ Spinoff
	
	
			


			
			
	

									Shane Mahood/Prime
	

		
	
				

	The series premiere of “Neagley” drops on Prime Video on Sept. 16, and with it comes a new batch of butt-kicking characters to the “Reacher” universe.

	Maria Sten returns as Frances Neagley, the Chicago private investigator and former military protégé of Jack Reacher. She’s joined by Greyston Holt as Detective Hudson Riley, Adeline Rudolph as Renée Birdwhistle and more. Jack Reacher (Alan Ritchson) himself even makes a guest appearance to fight alongside his mentee. 

	The eight-episode inaugural season follows Neagley as she leads her crew on an action-packed quest to uncover what really happened to her friend Tommy after he joined a mysterious cult. Based on the characters created by Lee Child, Neagley will use everything she’s learned from Jack Reacher and her time as a member of the 110 Special Investigators in her pursuit of justice. 

	Read below for Variety‘s breakdown of the new and familiar faces.


			
			
	Frances Neagley (Maria Sten)
			
										
					Image Credit: Jasper Savage/Prime				
					
				

	The series namesake, Frances Neagley, is a no-nonsense private investigator who ​​puts herself on a dangerous path to uncover a menacing evil. 

	What else you’ve seen her in: “Reacher,” “Swamp Thing” and “Channel Zero”

		
			
			
	Detective Hudson Riley (Greyston Holt)
			
										
					Image Credit: Robin Cymbaly/Prime				
					
				

	The black sheep in his family of criminals, Detective Hudson Riley sees Neagley’s investigation into her friend’s questionable death as the perfect opportunity to prove himself as an honest and hardworking cop. 

	What you‘ve seen him in: “The Night Agent,” “Lou” and “House of Chains” 

		
			
			
	Keno (Jasper Jones)
			
										
					Image Credit: Sabrina Lantos/Prime				
					
				

	Keno is an orphaned street kid who survived foster care and juvenile detention systems, but Neagley sees faith in him. Together, they will redirect the course of his life and fight for justice for Tommy. 

	What you’ve  seen him in: “Bleeding,” “To Die For” and “King Ivory”

		
			
			
	Renée Birdwhistle (Adeline Rudolph)
			
										
					Image Credit: Shane Mahood/Prime				
					
				

	Renée Birdwhistle is tired of being an administrative assistant and is ready to become a private investigator herself. Working with Neagley on Tommy’s case, she hopes she’ll uncover answers about her own brother’s disappearance. 

	What you’ve seen her in: “Mortal Kombat II,” Resident Evil,” “Chilling Adventures of Sabrina” and “Hellboy: The Crooked Man”

		
			
			
	Pierce Woodrow (Matthew Del Negro)
			
										
					Image Credit: Getty Images				
					
				

	Pierce Woodrow is the eye candy behind Invection Pharmaceuticals, but that’s no longer enough. His company, built on the promise to revolutionize trauma treatment, is running out of time before he needs to deliver results. 

	What you‘ve seen him in: “Free Bert,” “Mayor of Kingstown” and “Scandal”

		
			
			
	Lawrence Cole (Damon Herriman)
			
										
					Image Credit: Getty Images for TV WEEK Logie A				
					
				

	Lawrence Cole is not the simple farmer he appears to be. The self-fashioned prophet’s charming persona and care for his crops mask a deadly secret. 

	What you’ve seen him in: “Better Man,” “Together,” “The Little Death” and “Nightingale”

		
			
			
	Jack Reacher (Alan Ritchson)
			
										
					Image Credit: Jasper Savage/Prime				
					
				

	Jack Reacher returns to deliver advice to his protégé. Former Military Police Major and elite investigator, he used to be Neagley’s commanding officer and is one of the few people in the world she trusts. 

	What you’ve seen him in: “Reacher,” “War Machine,” “Fast X” and “The Ministry of Ungentlemanly Warfare”

		
			
			
	Arvid Rawlings (Peter Outerbridge)
			
										
					Image Credit: Getty Images				
					
				

	Arvid Rawlings is a mastermind in crime. He has citizenship in nine countries, a privately held biotech empire and mercenaries at his disposal. He especially doesn’t like it when his operations are threatened. 

	What you’ve seen him in: “Saw IV,” “Cool Runnings,” “Lucky Number Slevin” and “Silent Hill: Revelation”

title: Paramount Told Negotiators, 'We're Done,' Next 48 Hours Critical
description:
Paramount
                          After Saying 'We're Done,' Studio is Back Negotiating
body:
Paramount
                          After Saying 'We're Done,' Studio is Back Negotiating
                      
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Paramount told California officials negotiating a settlement Tuesday, "we're done" ... and said the studio was moving out of California, but our sources now say they are back at the bargaining table, but the clock is running out.
      
    
            Sources directly involved in the negotiation tell TMZ ... State and L.A. officials were planning on a statement from Paramount Tuesday, announcing its move out of Cali. But, one key source says, "We're back in a constructive place, but still in a red zone." The source adds, "It's by no means terminal, but the next 48 hour are critical." We're told if a settlement is possible, it's gonna come in the next 2 days ... otherwise, it's not going to happen.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Sources describe the negotiations as "tense."
      

            Paramount's threats center on a lawsuit brought by the California Attorney General and other states, trying to block the studio's acquisition of Warner Bros.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            David Ellison has been threatening to leave the State unless the A.G. backs off.
      
    
            Our sources would not discuss details of the negotiations, other than to say the goal is "compromise."
